subject: Re: Follow-up: Access controls & data handling (RBAC, support access, data residency)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintrust.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Access controls & data handling (RBAC, support access, data residency)

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so your security and infra teams have what they need for internal review.

Recap (from our side):
- You asked focused questions about PII handling, data retention, and logging for requests that touch customer content.
- Primary concerns: role-based access for FinTrust users, least-privilege access for Redwood support, break-glass procedures and audit trail, and data residency for EU-based accounts.
- You requested an initial support-access matrix and a short summary of our RBAC model and break-glass controls.

What I’m attaching:
- support_access_matrix.xlsx (high-level mapping of Redwood roles vs. access to customer data)
- redwood_rbac_design.pdf (overview of RBAC, service accounts, and least-privilege enforcement)

Short answers to the items you called out:
- PII: We treat all customer-provided content as confidential. Models run in isolated inference environments; we offer options to disable data retention on hosted requests and have private deployment options for full data isolation.
- Data retention: By default we retain logs for 90 days for telemetry; content retention is configurable per-customer. We can commit to shorter retention windows under contract and provide configurable TTLs for cached KV to meet compliance needs.
- Logging & audit: All access to customer data is logged with unique request IDs, user/service principals, and reason codes. Logs are immutable and available via the console and an audit API; we also integrate with customers' SIEMs via secure log delivery.
- RBAC & least privilege: Fine-grained roles (Admin, Engineering, Support, ReadOnly) with attribute-based conditions for resource scoping (org, project, model). Support access requires explicit Just-In-Time elevation and is time-limited by default.
- Break-glass: Emergency access is gated by multi-party approval and generates a high-fidelity audit event with the justification, approver identity, and automated notifications to your security mailbox.
- Data residency: Hosted options include regional model serving (US/EU/APAC). For regulated workloads we recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated and can provide on-prem or VPC deployments to satisfy residency requirements.

Next steps I propose:
1) Dev to confirm technical details on break-glass workflow and provide a short sequence diagram. (Dev, can you take this?)
2) Send the matrix to your security team; happy to join a review call next week.
3) If procurement is ready, I can share indicative contract language for retention and support scoping.

Availability: I have 30/31 Mar slots in the afternoon PST if you want a joint security + infra session.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: support_access_matrix.xlsx, redwood_rbac_design.pdf

Thanks Marissa — that recap helps. A few clarifying items from our security and compliance reviewers: 

1) Can you confirm whether 'disable data retention' means no request content is written to any persistent storage (including backups)? We need a clear affirmative or a description of where ephemeral caches may persist.
2) For support JIT elevation: is there an approval SLA (e.g., 15 minutes for Level 1 incidents)? Who can approve from Redwood?
3) Break-glass: will the approval be recorded in an immutable log and is that log exportable to our SIEM (we use Splunk)?
4) Data residency: our legal prefers EU-only processing for EU customer content. What's the lead time and cost delta for provisioning an EU-only dedicated pool?

Procurement copied on this thread — they may open an initial SOW/term-sheet once security is satisfied.

Also: could you send the SOC2 summary and any previous customer attestations about support access?

Appreciate it,
Alex
Director of Infrastructure
FinTrust

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Access controls & data handling (RBAC, support access, data residency)

Alex — thanks for the follow-ups, see answers inline below and a couple of attached docs.

1) Persistence of request content:
- We do not write request content to persistent backups when 'data retention' is disabled for a customer's account. Ephemeral caches (in-memory KV) may exist for serving performance but are purged per the configured TTL and are not included in backup snapshots. We can include explicit language in the contract: "no persistent storage of request content" when retention == 0.

2) Support JIT elevation SLA & approvers:
- Default workflow: support engineer requests elevation -> automated ticket routed to on-call support lead -> approval window configurable. For enterprise/Dedicated customers we offer a 15-minute SLA for Level 1 incident elevation as part of an operational addendum. Approvers are designated Redwood staff (Support On-Call Lead, SOC Manager) and their identities/roles are recorded in the audit log.

3) Break-glass logging & SIEM integration:
- All break-glass events are emitted to the audit log and can be streamed to your Splunk instance via secure syslog or S3 push. Logs include approver identity, timestamp, justification, and affected resources.

4) EU-only processing & lead time:
- For Dedicated pools: typical provisioning lead time is 4-6 weeks depending on capacity. Cost delta is usually in the 10-20% range depending on size and reserved commitment; we’ll scope exact numbers once we have target throughput.

Attachments added: SOC2-summary.pdf (summary and evidence references)

Next steps:
- Dev will produce the sequence diagram and a short technical note on where ephemeral caches live and how they are purged.
- I can schedule a security review call — Alex, are you available Thurs 5 Mar, 10:00 AM CET / 04:00 AM PST? If not, propose a couple of times and I’ll coordinate.

Thanks —
Marissa

Hi Alex — quick technical note / sequence on the break-glass + RBAC flow you asked for. Attaching a short diagram as PDF (redwood_rbac_design.pdf) and a support access matrix.

Sequence (high level):
1) Support engineer opens a ticket and requests JIT elevation (includes reason and ticket id).
2) The request is routed to the on-call approver; approver authenticates via SSO and must provide MFA.
3) Approval is recorded in the audit service (immutable append-only store) and an ephemeral access token is minted for the support principal scoped to the specific customer resource.
4) Token TTL is short (default 15 minutes) and token usage is logged per-request (request id, api call, resource).
5) At expiry or manual revoke, the token is invalidated and the session record is preserved in the audit trail.

Notes on caches:
- KV/prefix caches are in-memory on the serving nodes and sharded per-tenant. They are not part of persistent backups. Cache purge is triggered on TTL, model/weights redeploys, and explicit admin actions.

We can generate a one-page SAML & auth flow diagram for your infra team if that helps. Happy to join the call next week.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
